name: Destitute: Migrant with terminated income in first month → true
description: Migrant farm worker household in first month of certification, only income is from a terminated source received before application date. Should be destitute.

name: Destitute: Not first month of certification → false
description: Migrant farm worker with terminated income, but benefit month is NOT the first month of the certification period. Should not be destitute.

name: Destitute: Non-migrant household → false
description: Household in first month of certification with terminated income, but no migrant farm worker. Should not be destitute.

name: Destitute: New source income >$25 not received by deadline → true
description: Migrant farm worker in first month, only income is from a new source, amount >$25, and pay date is after the 10-day deadline. Should be destitute.

name: Destitute: New source income ≤$25 → false
description: Migrant farm worker in first month, only income from new source but amount is $25 (not more than $25). Should NOT be destitute because new source must exceed $25.

name: Destitute: New source received within deadline → false
description: Migrant farm worker in first month, new source income >$25 but pay date is BEFORE the 10-day deadline (Jan 25). Should NOT be destitute.

name: Destitute: Mixed terminated + new source income → true
description: Migrant farm worker in first month with a combination: one terminated source received before application AND one new source >$25 not received by deadline. Should be destitute per 4.406.A.3.

name: Destitute: Has non-qualifying income alongside terminated → false
description: Migrant in first month with one terminated income AND one regular (neither terminated nor new source) income received this month. The regular income fails the destitute source test, so should NOT be destitute.

name: Circularity: isOnlyHouseholdParentOfDependentChild inner parent count
description: A 20-year-old full-time college student is the sole parent of a 7-year-old child. Both prepare food with the household (so they are part of it via food-prep, not mandatory membership). The child is older than the under-six care exemption, so the student must qualify through the single-parent student exemption via isOnlyHouseholdParentOfDependentChild. That should make them not an ineligible student, which should make isPartOfHousehold true. However, the inner parent-count filter in isOnlyHouseholdParentOfDependentChild requires caregiverId/isPartOfHousehold — which for the student depends on not being an ineligible student, which depends on this very exemption. This creates a circularity that causes null propagation. The fix is to count the current candidate student in the inner parent count even before their isPartOfHousehold is resolved.

name: Circularity: hasNonparentParentalControlOfDependentChildWithoutHouseholdParentOrSpouse inner parent count
description: A 20-year-old full-time college student has non-parent parental control over a 7-year-old child (e.g., aunt or grandparent). No natural/adoptive/stepparent is in the household and the caregiver has no spouse. The child is older than the under-six care exemption, so the student must qualify through the parental-control branch of the single-parent student exemption via hasNonparentParentalControlOfDependentChildWithoutHouseholdParentOrSpouse. The inner parent-count filter checks caregiverId/isPartOfHousehold for any parent of the child — if a parent were also a student, this would create a circularity. This test verifies the non-parent parental control path resolves correctly.

name: Complex 5-member household with multiple income sources, elderly member, and varied deductions
description: A 5-member household: married couple (ages 40 and 38) with two children (ages 14 and 8) in K-12, and an elderly grandparent (age 68) who is a veteran with a physical disability. The head of household earns $1,800/mo wages; the spouse earns $450 biweekly; the grandparent receives $800/mo Social Security and $200/mo VA benefits. Expenses include a $1,100 mortgage, $150 heating fuel, $100 electricity, $50 water, $400 dependent care, $150 prescription drugs for the elderly member, and $200 child support. Resources total $1,500 across three accounts. Four caregiver relationships link both parents to both children. The household qualifies under ECE with heating/cooling utility allowance, dependent care deduction, excess medical deduction, and excess shelter deduction.
